newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt ends week with good underlying bid tone.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt ends week with good underlying bid tone.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (JUN) 92.88 (PREV 92.84) 90-DAYS 7.01 (PREV 7.03)
OVERNIGHT CASH 6.50 PCT (PREV 6.55) US 5-YR 6.50 (PREV 6.53)
* NZ debt ends week bid after soft retail trade data
* Offshore buying through session helps bonds
* Bonds seen dictated to next week by U.S. pre-FOMC trade
New Zealand debt ended the week with an underlying bid tone across the curve on Friday as the market took heart from soft retail trade data and offshore buying during the session.

In the money market, the 90-day bank bills ended two pips stronger at 7.01 percent, while the front futures contract gained four on the day to close at 92.88. Flows in the futures were substantial, with 4,131 June and 804 September contracts traded.
Earlier, Statistics New Zealand (SNZ) said seasonally adjusted retail sales fell one percent in the March quarter, following a fall of 0.3 percent in the December quarter.
In real terms, seasonally adjusted sales fell 0.8 percent in the quarter, against general market expectations of a 0.1 percent fall.

"It was obviously a very weak number. The economy is falling into a hole pretty fast. Our impression is it is going to be a reasonably large negative GDP growth number for the first quarter now -- the first one in 17 quarters," one Wellington chief dealer said.
March quarter GDP data is due on June 30, three days after the Reserve Bank's next monetary policy statement.
Bankers Trust NZ chief economist David Plank said the retail data was consistent with the RBNZ's easing bias.
"We still see the RBNZ easing in the 27 June monetary policy statement, by at least 50 basis points in interest rate terms from its March assumptions," he wrote in a commentary.
In March the RBNZ assumed 90-day bank bills at 7.5 percent and the currency's Trade-Weighted Index (TWI) at 68.0.
On Friday the TWI was closing fairly steady at 67.77.

Dealers said the bond yield curve, particularly in the long end, would be susceptible at the start of next week to movements in U.S. Treasuries. That market is generally edgy ahead of the Federal Reserve's Tuesday meeting, with sentiment still mixed over the possibility of a further hike in official interest rates.
-- Catherine McCaw, Wellington newsroom (64 4) 471 4275
